selection_rationale: Reference mounting hardware a French studio, radio or location-sound student meets every day: K&M boom stands (the 210/9 is already a TekPractice catalog item), the Yellowtec m!ka broadcast arm used in radio studios, the Neumann EA 87 and Rycote InVision USM studio suspensions, Rode and Rycote windshield/blimp systems, carbon boom poles from Rode and Ambient, two classic pop filters (K&M metal-free nylon, Stedman metal), and an SKB roto-moulded 19-inch rack case. All specs come from manufacturer pages or manufacturer PDFs read this session; WebSearch was exhausted so no retailer cross-checks could be found by search.

devices.technology: Steel tripod microphone stand with zinc die-cast base, foldable legs, clutch height adjustment and 2-piece telescopic boom arm locked by a T-bar screw
devices.why_it_is_a_classic: K&M's datasheet calls it a more compact version of the classic 210/2 and says the 210/9, like the 210/2, sets the standard for professional microphone boom stands. It is the generic boom stand found in most European studios and venues.
typical_uses: vocal and instrument miking in studio

key_specs.base: socket with foldable legs; zinc die-cast base

manuals.title: Aufstellanleitung für K&M-Mikrofonstative (covers 21090 and other boom stands)

devices.notes: Two manufacturer documents (web page and PDF datasheet) agree on all specs. The middle block of the article number encodes the thread: -300 is 3/8" BSW, -500 is 5/8"-27 UNS, so a 5/8" mic clip needs an adapter on the standard -300 version.

tekpractice.sim_value_reason: No signal connectors; useful only as scene furniture and for 3/8" vs 5/8" thread-adapter lessons.

devices.technology: Low-level steel tripod microphone stand with zinc die-cast base, foldable legs, clutch height adjustment and 2-piece telescopic boom arm

key_specs.special_features: low-level microphone stand; zinc die-cast base

devices.technology: Spring-balanced steel desk arm with table clamp and supplied XLR cable

key_specs.table_clamp_range: 10 to 51 mm / ø 15 to ø 51 mm

devices.model: m!ka Mic Arm (M / XL / XS, standard and On Air versions)
devices.technology: Aluminium-tube broadcast microphone arm with hidden internal linkage and coil springs, internal mic cable, optional On Air version with a 12-LED ring fed by a hybrid cable (12-24 V DC)
devices.why_it_is_a_classic: The m!ka arm is a staple of European radio studios; its On Air version integrates the red 'on air' indicator and the mic cable in one arm, which ties the arm into the studio tally logic.

key_specs.mount_post: ø16 mm post, 66 mm insertion (ø51 mm column)
key_specs.material: Sturdy aluminum tube construction, silk-mat anodized finish (aluminum or black)
key_specs.on_air_feed: Feed +12...+24V to activate ON AIR Signalling. Current drain approx. 40 mA (regulated DC)
key_specs.on_air_hybrid_cable: hot (red), cold (blue), shield for microphone audio; +12...+24V (orange), 0V (black) for on-air signalling
key_specs.on_air_indicator: 12 LED array, constant current source; dual color (red and white) on current On Air arms
key_specs.cable_tails: Open-ended cable tails; cable juts out by >450mm (top) and >1500mm (bottom) per 2016 drawings

manuals.title: m!ka Mic Arm On Air Wiring Instruction
m!ka Microphone Arms overview and dimensional drawings

devices.notes: Two Yellowtec PDFs and two web pages agree on the 5/8" thread and LED feed voltage. The m!ka overview page states 'up to 1.5kg' (XL max. 1.2kg) while the 2021 PDF table states max mic weight 2kg for M/XS; recorded as a conflict. The m!ka overview page also says the On Air lower end uses XLR-5 and the upper XLR-3 but that XLR connectors are not included, so connectors[] is left empty. 'dc-power' is a proposed signal id. The wiring sheet covers older article numbers YT3204/YT3205/YT3200/YT3201.

conflicts.note: The 2016 dimensional drawings in the same PDF show a 0,5-1,5kg range, matching the web page.

tekpractice.sim_value_reason: On Air version carries mic audio plus a 12-24 V DC tally feed in one hybrid cable: a good on-air light / GPIO tally lesson in a radio scene.
